:::{#thm-add-outside-span}
#### Adding a vector outside the span keeps a list independent

If $\vecf{v}_1, \ldots, \vecf{v}_k$ are linearly independent
(@def-linearly-independent)
and $\vecf{w}$ is not in $\operatorname{span}\cb{\vecf{v}_1, \ldots, \vecf{v}_k}$
(@def-span),
then $\vecf{v}_1, \ldots, \vecf{v}_k, \vecf{w}$ are linearly independent.

:::

::: proof

Suppose $c_1 \vecf{v}_1 + \cdots + c_k \vecf{v}_k + d\,\vecf{w} = \vzero$.

**The coefficient $d$ is $0$.**
If $d \neq 0$, then

$$
\ba
\vecf{w}
&= \frac{1}{d}\,\paren{d\,\vecf{w}}
&& \text{(} d \neq 0 \text{)}
\\
&= \frac{1}{d}\,\paren{-c_1 \vecf{v}_1 - \cdots - c_k \vecf{v}_k}
&& \text{(solve the supposed equation for } d\,\vecf{w} \text{)}
\\
&= \paren{-\frac{c_1}{d}}\,\vecf{v}_1 + \cdots + \paren{-\frac{c_k}{d}}\,\vecf{v}_k,
&& \text{(distribute } \tfrac{1}{d} \text{)}
\ea
$$

which puts $\vecf{w}$ in $\operatorname{span}\cb{\vecf{v}_1, \ldots, \vecf{v}_k}$,
contrary to the assumption.

**The other coefficients are $0$.**
With $d = 0$, the equation reads
$c_1 \vecf{v}_1 + \cdots + c_k \vecf{v}_k = \vzero$,
so every $c_i = 0$,
because $\vecf{v}_1, \ldots, \vecf{v}_k$ are linearly independent.

:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

:::{#exm-add-outside-span}
#### Adding $(0, 0, 1)$ to two independent vectors in $\reals^3$

The vectors $(1, 0, 0)$ and $(0, 1, 0)$ are linearly independent,
and their span is the plane $z = 0$ (@exm-span).
The vector $(0, 0, 1)$ has third entry $1$, so it is not in that plane,
and by @thm-add-outside-span
the three vectors $(1, 0, 0)$, $(0, 1, 0)$, $(0, 0, 1)$ are linearly independent.
Adding $(1, 1, 0)$ instead would not work:
$(1, 1, 0)$ is in the span,
and $(1, 0, 0) + (0, 1, 0) - (1, 1, 0) = \vzero$.

:::
